label: History
value: Aunt Em originally came to live on the Kansas prairie.
unit: Aunt Em originally came to live on the Kansas prairie as a young, pretty wife, though the drab environment eventually transformed her into a gray, somber woman. When a severe cyclone struck their farm, she quickly took shelter in the cyclone cellar, but the storm swept away their house with Dorothy inside. Months later, she was joyfully reunited with Dorothy when her niece suddenly appeared on the farm after traveling back from the Land of Oz. She was later left at home in Kansas to take care of the farm and watch over the hired men when her frail husband, Uncle Henry, took Dorothy on a voyage to Australia.

label: History
value: Billina was raised on a farm in the United States.
unit: Raised on a farm in the United States, Billina was named Bill by a farm boy who mistook her gender before she was swept out to sea. She wakes up floating in a hen-coop alongside Dorothy, and the two introduce themselves and make landfall on a beach. Together, they navigate encounters with the Wheelers, discover the mechanical copper man Tiktok, and make their way to the palace of the Land of Ev. After Dorothy is locked away and Billina is sent to the chicken-house, Dorothy rescues Billina from a fight with a speckled rooster, and Billina joins Ozma's expedition to rescue Ev's royal family from the Nome King. During the journey, Billina lays a daily egg and secretly overhears the Nome King explain the secret behind his ornament transformations while hiding beneath his throne. Exploiting the king's terror of eggs, Billina bargains for her turn in the enchanted palace, where she successfully disenchants the royal family of Ev and the citizens of Oz. During a subsequent battle, her eggs are used to blind and terrify the Nome King, allowing Dorothy to seize his magical belt. On the return trip, Billina realizes a tin pig whistle is actually the transformed Tin Woodman and restores him, after which she travels with Dorothy and their companions to the Emerald City for a grand celebration before Dorothy departs for Australia.

label: History
value: The Highly Magnified, Thoroughly Educated Woggle-Bug was born an ordinary woggle-bug.
unit: Born an ordinary woggle-bug, the Highly Magnified, Thoroughly Educated Woggle-Bug gained his exceptional size and knowledge after spending three years in a school-house hearth listening to a schoolmaster before being enlarged on a magnifying screen. Escaping to a grove of trees, he later joined Tip, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and Jack Pumpkinhead on their journey to the Emerald City, even suggesting how to repair the Saw-Horse's broken leg. Though his persistent puns annoyed his companions, he accompanied them through various magical illusions to the city, where they were trapped by General Jinjur's forces inside the royal palace. Flying out of the city on the newly constructed Gump machine, he ended up stranded in a giant Jackdaw nest, where he discovered a diamond necklace and gifted it to the Tin Woodman. During the ordeal, he took shelter beneath the Scarecrow's straw to hide from attacking birds, and he later successfully used one of Dr. Nikidik's Wishing Pills to repair the Gump's broken wings. After reaching Glinda the Good and witnessing Tip's restoration to Princess Ozma, he accompanied Ozma on her adventures leading up to her taking the throne, ultimately continuing to associate with her and her companions in the Emerald City.

unit: Born an ordinary woggle-bug, the Highly Magnified, Thoroughly Educated Woggle-Bug gained his exceptional size and knowledge after spending three years in a school-house hearth listening to a schoolmaster before being enlarged on a magnifying screen. Escaping to a grove of trees, he later joined Tip, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and Jack Pumpkinhead on their journey to the Emerald City, even suggesting how to repair the Saw-Horse's broken leg. Though his persistent puns annoyed his companions, he accompanied them through various magical illusions to the city, where they were trapped by General Jinjur's forces inside the royal palace. Flying out of the city on the newly constructed Gump machine, he ended up stranded in a giant Jackdaw nest, where he discovered a diamond necklace and gifted it to the Tin Woodman. During the ordeal, he took shelter beneath the Scarecrow's straw to hide from attacking birds, and he later successfully used one of Dr. Nikidik's Wishing Pills to repair the Gump's broken wings. After reaching Glinda the Good and witnessing Tip's restoration to Princess Ozma, he accompanied Ozma on her adventures leading up to her taking the throne, ultimately continuing to associate with her and her companions in the Emerald City.

label: Quote
value: Bug said: "I have never ceased to congratulate myself for escaping while I was Highly Magnified; for even my excessive knowledge would have proved of little use to me had I remained a tiny, insignificant insect."

label: Quote
value: Bug said: "If the Pumpkinhead is to ride, why not use one of his legs to make a leg for the horse that carries him? I judge that both are made of wood."

label: Quote
value: Bug said: “But you were the King until she came,” said the Woggle-Bug, strutting up and down with his hands in his pockets; “so it appears to me that she is the interloper instead of you.”

label: Quote
value: Bug said: “As for me,” said the Woggle-Bug, “I think that I could live for some time on Jack Pumpkinhead. Not that I prefer pumpkins for food; but I believe they are somewhat nutritious, and Jack’s head is large and plump.”

label: Quote
value: Bug said: “You have; and I’ve restrained a good many of them,” replied the insect. “But there are opportunities for so many excellent puns in our language that, to an educated person like myself, the temptation to express them is almost irresistible.”

label: Personality
value: The Cowardly Lion considers himself a coward.
unit: The Cowardly Lion is a wild beast who considers himself a coward and is afraid of everything, though he comes to know himself as being as brave as any beast that ever lived. He is recognized by others for his courage and loyalty as a comrade. Throughout his journey, he is driven by a deep motivation to obtain courage from the Wizard Oz so that his life will be bearable and he can truly become the King of Beasts as men call him. He specifically desires the type of courage that allows him to forget his fears. Despite his inherent bravery, he harbors specific fears of falling, Kalidahs, and being in danger.

label: History
value: The Lion believed he was born a coward.
unit: Believing he was born a coward, the Lion spent his youth roaring loudly to terrify other creatures into fleeing from him. While traveling through a thick forest, he attacked Dorothy Gale's companions, but after Dorothy slapped his nose and called him out, he admitted his secret lack of courage and agreed to join her journey to see the Great Oz. Throughout their trek along the yellow brick road, he aided the group by carrying them across deep ditches, swimming a raft through swift river currents, and offering to fight on their behalf. After falling victim to a field of magical sleeping poppies, he was rescued by thousands of field mice harnessed to a wooden truck built by the Tin Woodman. Upon reaching the Emerald City, he encountered Oz as a terrifying Ball of Fire and was tasked with slaying the Wicked Witch of the West. During their quest in the West, he was captured and imprisoned by the Wicked Witch, but Dorothy secretly sustained him until she melted the Witch. Following their return to the Emerald City, Oz admitted he was a humbug but granted the Lion a potion for courage. Later, while traveling to the South Country, the Lion decapitated a giant spider-like monster terrorizing a grand forest, leading the local animals to joyfully proclaim him their King. He eventually accompanied Dorothy to Glinda's castle before she returned to Kansas, after which he ruled over the forest as the King of Beasts. Later, he joined Princess Ozma's grand procession to the Land of Ev to rescue the captive royal family from the Nome King. During the confrontation in the underground palace, the Lion actively defended Dorothy against the Nome army, helping secure their victory and the recovery of their enchanted friends before returning to the Emerald City for a celebratory reunion.

label: History
value: Dorothy is an orphan
unit: Dorothy is an orphan from Kansas who originally lived on the dry gray prairies with her Uncle Henry and Aunt Em. Her adventures begin when a severe cyclone carries her inside her house to the Land of Oz, accidentally landing on and killing the Wicked Witch of the East. She is given the dead witch's silver shoes and travels along the yellow brick road to the Emerald City, where the Great Oz refuses to send her back to Kansas unless she destroys the Wicked Witch of the West. Along the way, Dorothy forms close friendships with the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion, and she eventually kills the Wicked Witch of the West by throwing a bucket of water on her. After Oz leaves without her in a hot-air balloon, Dorothy reaches the castle of Glinda the Good Witch, who explains that the magical silver shoes can transport her anywhere; Dorothy uses them to return home to her aunt and uncle. During a later voyage across the ocean to Australia with Uncle Henry, another storm blows Dorothy overboard inside a chicken coop with a talking yellow hen named Billina. They drift to the shore of Ev, where Dorothy discovers a clockwork man named Tiktok, whom she winds up to act as her defender. She is imprisoned in the palace of Princess Langwidere, but is rescued when Princess Ozma of Oz arrives with Dorothy's old companions. Joining Ozma's quest to free the royal family of Ev from the Nome King, Dorothy ventures into his underground realm. When the King traps her companions as transformed ornaments, Dorothy uses her guesses to restore Prince Evring, and Billina subsequently restores the rest of the party. After the Scarecrow throws eggs to subdue the egg-phobic Nome King, Dorothy seizes his magical belt to ensure their safe escape back to Ev. After celebrating the coronation of Ev's new king, Dorothy travels with Ozma to the Emerald City, where she is crowned a Princess of Oz.

label: History
value: General Jinjur spent her youth making beds.
unit: Before her political rise, General Jinjur spent her youth making beds and washing dishes for her mother. Seeking a more aristocratic life, she assembled an Army of Revolt composed of young women and successfully captured the Emerald City, driving the Scarecrow from his throne. She later summoned the witch Mombi to assist in defending her position and fought a battle against the forces of Glinda the Sorceress. After refusing to relinquish power, Jinjur was captured during an aerial assault led by Glinda and Princess Ozma, which ended her revolt. Following her defeat, she eventually reencountered her former foes and allies as they traveled across the desert to the Emerald City.

value: General Jinjur said: “There!” said she; “it is time for me to go. Carry that basket for me and help yourself to its contents if you are hungry.”

value: General Jinjur said: “Oh, no”, said Jinjur. “What man would oppose a girl, or dare to harm her? And there is not an ugly face in my entire Army.”

label: Quote
value: General Jinjur said: “To think,” she moaned, “that after having ruled as Queen, and lived in a palace, I must go back to scrubbing floors and churning butter again! It is too horrible to think of! I will never consent!”

label: Quote
value: General Jinjur said: "I have taken it, as you see; so just now I am the Queen, and all who oppose me are guilty of treason, and must be punished by the law you have just mentioned."

label: Quote
value: General Jinjur said: "The enemy is still outside the walls, so we must try to gain time by engaging them in parley. Go you with a flag of truce to Glinda and ask her why she has dared to invade my dominions, and what are her demands."

label: History
value: Glinda is a Good Witch of the South.
unit: Glinda is a beautiful Good Witch of the South who has retained a youthful appearance despite living for many years. When Dorothy Gale and her companions reached her castle seeking aid, Glinda agreed to help by using the Golden Cap to return the Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, and Cowardly Lion to their respective realms, while informing Dorothy that her Silver Shoes possessed the power to carry her back to Kansas. Later, Glinda welcomed a new group of travelers seeking to liberate the Emerald City, revealing to them that Princess Ozma was the rightful ruler. Glinda marched her army to the Emerald City, captured the transformed witch Mombi following a desert pursuit, and forced Mombi to break the enchantment that restored Tip into Princess Ozma. Glinda subsequently led an aerial assault on the Emerald City to capture General Jinjur and end the revolt, enabling Ozma's coronation. When Dorothy later returned to Oz and wished to rejoin her sick uncle in Australia without losing the magic belt, Dorothy and Ozma consulted Glinda, who advised that Ozma wear the belt to wish Dorothy directly to Australia.

When Dorothy Gale and her companions reached her castle seeking aid, Glinda agreed to help by using the Golden Cap to return the Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, and Cowardly Lion to their respective realms, while informing Dorothy that her Silver Shoes possessed the power to carry her back to Kansas. Later, Glinda welcomed a new group of travelers seeking to liberate the Emerald City, revealing to them that Princess Ozma was the rightful ruler. Glinda marched her army to the Emerald City, captured the transformed witch Mombi following a desert pursuit, and forced Mombi to break the enchantment that restored Tip into Princess Ozma. Glinda subsequently led an aerial assault on the Emerald City to capture General Jinjur and end the revolt, enabling Ozma's coronation. When Dorothy later returned to Oz and wished to rejoin her sick uncle in Australia without losing the magic belt, Dorothy and Ozma consulted Glinda, who advised that Ozma wear the belt to wish Dorothy directly to Australia.

label: Quote
value: Glinda said: “By means of the Golden Cap I shall command the Winged Monkeys to carry you to the gates of the Emerald City,” said Glinda, “for it would be a shame to deprive the people of so wonderful a ruler.”

label: Quote
value: Glinda said: "yet I cannot understand how I have been defeated so easily by an old Witch who knows far less of magic than I do myself."

label: Quote
value: Glinda said: “That is true,” replied the Sorceress, slowly. “But the Emerald City is now ruled by General Jinjur, who has caused herself to be proclaimed Queen. What right have I to oppose her?”

label: Quote
value: Glinda said: “Then,” decided Glinda, “I will march with my army to the Emerald City, and take Mombi prisoner. After that we can, perhaps, force her to tell the truth about Ozma.”

label: Quote
value: Glinda said: “I am quite obstinate myself,” returned the Sorceress, with a sweet smile. “so I do not fear Mombi in the least. Today I will make all necessary preparations, and we will march upon the Emerald City at daybreak tomorrow.”

label: History
value: The Great Oz is known to the inhabitants of the land as a powerful ruler.
unit: Known to the inhabitants of the land as a powerful ruler, the Great Oz requires visitors to the Emerald City to wear green-tinted spectacles before granting them individual audiences in his palace. When Dorothy and her companions seek his help, he assumes a different magical form for each visitor—appearing as a giant Head, a winged Lady, a five-eyed Beast, and a Ball of Fire—and refuses to fulfill their wishes until they destroy the Wicked Witch of the West. Upon their return, Toto knocks over a screen in the throne room, exposing Oz as a non-magical ventriloquist and ordinary man from Omaha. After admitting he is a humbug who has been deceiving everyone, he promises to grant the group's requests the next day.

label: Quote
value: Great Oz said: "I have fooled everyone so long that I thought I should never be found out. It was a great mistake my ever letting you into the Throne Room. Usually I will not see even my subjects, and so they believe I am something terrible."

label: Quote
value: Great Oz said: "I can throw the sound of my voice wherever I wish, so that you thought it was coming out of the Head. Here are the other things I used to deceive you."

label: Quote
value: Great Oz said: "When I grew up I became a ventriloquist, and at that I was very well trained by a great master. I can imitate any kind of a bird or beast."

label: Quote
value: Great Oz said: "I’m not much of a magician, as I said; but if you will come to me tomorrow morning, I will stuff your head with brains. I cannot tell you how to use them, however; you must find that out for yourself."

label: Quote
value: Great Oz said: "I think you are wrong to want a heart. It makes most people unhappy. If you only knew it, you are in luck not to have a heart."

label: History
value: Green Whiskers served as a Royal Army
unit: Green Whiskers previously served as a good Royal Army during the reign of the Wonderful Wizard. When Jack Pumpkinhead and the Saw-Horse arrived at the Emerald City, Green Whiskers fitted them with green spectacles, escorted Jack to the Scarecrow, and later fetched Jellia Jamb to serve as an interpreter during their initial meeting. When General Jinjur's Army of Revolt attacked the city, the invaders discovered that Green Whiskers's gun was unloaded and quickly captured the Emerald City, prompting Green Whiskers to retreat to the palace to inform the Scarecrow.

label: History
value: The Guardian locked green-tinted spectacles onto Dorothy
unit: When Dorothy and her companions first arrived at the Emerald City, the Guardian locked green-tinted spectacles onto each traveler before leading them inside the gates. Later, when Dorothy's group departed for the South Country, they took their leave of him. He subsequently attached green spectacles to Jack Pumpkinhead and the Saw-Horse upon their arrival at the city and escorted Jack to see the Scarecrow. Shortly after, when General Jinjur's Army of Revolt marched on the Emerald City, the female rebels quickly overpowered the Guardian at the city gates using knitting needles.

label: Quote
value: Guardian said: “Don’t try, my dear,” he answered. “We should like to keep you with us, but if it is your wish to return to Kansas, I hope you will find a way.”

label: Quote
value: Guardian said: “Ouch!” cried the man; “I’m sorry I asked that question. But the answer is most convincing. Have you any errand, sir, in the Emerald City?”

label: Quote
value: Guardian said: "Here is a strange gentleman who doesn’t know why he has come to the Emerald City, or what he wants. Tell me, what shall we do with him?"

label: Quote
value: Guardian said: “I haven’t a pair in stock that will really cover those eyes up,” said the little man, with a sigh; “and your head is so big that I shall be obliged to tie the spectacles on.”

label: Quote
value: Guardian said: “Good gracious!” returned the surprised Guardian of the Gates; “what a nonsensical idea! Go home to your mothers, my good girls, and milk the cows and bake the bread. Don’t you know it’s a dangerous thing to conquer a city?”

value: The Guardian of the Gate loses control of the Emerald City's entrance to General Jinjur.
unit: The Guardian of the Gate loses control of the Emerald City's entrance to General Jinjur during her Army of Revolt's surprise assault. After Jinjur and her all-female army march upon the city, they swiftly overpower the Guardian at the gates using knitting needles. This sudden defeat allows Jinjur's forces to rush into the city and capture it without bloodshed.

label: History
value: The Gump once was a monarch of the forest.
unit: Once a monarch of the forest with legs that carried him swiftly, the Gump was killed and his mounted head was later used by Nick Chopper and Tip to construct a flying creature, which Tip brought to life using the Powder of Life. After the Woggle-Bug repaired his broken wings with a wishing pill, the Gump flew Tip and his companions to pursue the disguised witch Mombi across the desert and transport her back to camp after Glinda captured her. He was then used to launch an aerial assault on the Emerald City to capture General Jinjur, after which he was dismantled upon his own request.

label: History
value: The Saw-Horse was brought to life by Tip using Mombi's Powder of Life.
unit: Brought to life by the boy Tip using Mombi's magic Powder of Life, the Saw-Horse was fitted with wooden ears bored into its head so it could hear commands, along with a post hammered into its back to serve as a handhold. Tip guided the newly animated horse along the yellow brick road toward the Emerald City, but during a river crossing, the horse galloped off too quickly, snapping its tail off in Tip's hands and carrying Jack Pumpkinhead ahead to the city. Later, tied securely to the Saw-Horse, Tip, Jack, and the Scarecrow escaped the palace and plunged into a wide river before riding on to the Tin Woodman's palace. While continuing their journey, the Saw-Horse tripped in a rabbit hole and broke its leg, which was repaired using one of Jack's legs at the Woggle-Bug's suggestion. After flying out of Oz on a wooden Gump and becoming stranded in a giant Jackdaw nest, the Saw-Horse figured out how to fulfill the complex counting requirement for Dr. Nikidik's wishing pills, allowing the party to repair the Gump and fly to Glinda the Good. During a pursuit across the desert, Glinda rode the Saw-Horse to chase down Mombi, who had transformed into a massive Griffin, successfully capturing the witch when she collapsed from exhaustion. Following the restoration of Princess Ozma to the throne, Ozma had the Saw-Horse shod with plates of gold so its wooden legs would not wear out.

During a pursuit across the desert, Glinda rode the Saw-Horse to chase down Mombi, who had transformed into a massive Griffin, successfully capturing the witch when she collapsed from exhaustion. Following the restoration of Princess Ozma to the throne, Ozma had the Saw-Horse shod with plates of gold so its wooden legs would not wear out.

label: Quote
value: Horse said: “Well, I cannot claim any great experience in life,” the Saw-Horse answered for himself. “but I seem to learn very quickly, and often it occurs to me that I know more than any of those around me.”

label: Quote
value: Horse said: “Then it pleases me to be able to call you a fool, in return,” said the horse. “For I did not make the river, nor put it in our way; so only a term of, reproach is fit for one who becomes angry with me for falling into the water.”

label: Quote
value: Horse said: “Then I will do as you tell me,” replied the Saw-Horse, humbly. “But what happened to me, a moment ago? I don’t seem to be just right, someway.”

label: Quote
value: Horse said: “I’m off, too!” cried the Saw-Horse, turning and prancing with agitation; “for my wood is so dry it would burn like kindlings.”

label: Quote
value: Horse said: “I’ll have nothing more to do with that Pumpkinhead,” declared the Saw-Horse, viciously. “he loses his head too easily to suit me.”

After the successful rescue, he accompanied the group back to the Emerald City for a grand grand celebration.

unit: Born hungry, the Hungry Tiger eventually left the forest to join his friend, the Cowardly Lion. During the mission, he helped defend Dorothy alongside the Cowardly Lion and the Sawhorse when the angry Nome King attempted to capture her. After the successful rescue, he accompanied the group back to the Emerald City for a grand grand celebration.

label: Quote
value: Hungry Tiger said: "For my part, I'm a savage beast, and have an appetite for all sorts of poor little living creatures, from a chipmonk to fat babies."

label: Quote
value: Hungry Tiger said: "My, my! how good you would taste if I could only crunch you between my jaws. But don't worry. You would only appease my appetite for a moment; so it isn't worth while to eat you."

label: Quote
value: Hungry Tiger said: "Then," said the Tiger, yawning frightfully, "please to get me about thirty pounds of tenderloin steak, cooked rare, with a peck of boiled potatoes on the side, and five gallons of ice-cream for dessert."

label: Quote
value: Hungry Tiger said: "A bushel of them, hard boiled, might take a little of the edge off my appetite; but one egg isn't good for anything at all, that I know of."

label: Quote
value: Hungry Tiger said: "A nice, plump, juicy, tender, fat baby. But, of course, if I had one, my conscience would not allow me to eat it. So I'll have to be an ornament and forget my hunger."

label: History
value: Jack Pumpkinhead was constructed as a wooden dummy.
unit: Jack Pumpkinhead was constructed as a wooden dummy with a carved pumpkin head by the young boy Tip, who built him in the Gillikin region of Oz to prank the old sorceress Mombi. Mombi subsequently brought Jack to life using a magical powder. Fearing Mombi's plans to turn him into a statue, Tip fled with Jack toward the Emerald City. To facilitate their journey, Tip animated a wooden sawhorse for Jack to ride. Separated from Tip along the way, Jack arrived in the city first and formed a friendship with the Scarecrow after clearing up a language misunderstanding.

label: History
value: Jack escaped from the city when Jinjur's army invaded.
unit: When Jinjur's army invaded the city, Jack escaped alongside Tip, the Scarecrow, and the Tin Woodman on the Saw-Horse, though his jointed legs required occasional repair and replacement during their travels. After joining forces with the Woggle-Bug and the Queen of the Field Mice, Jack participated in an attempt to retake the palace, which resulted in the group becoming trapped inside. He was then carried aboard an animated flying Gump machine built on the palace roof. When the machine crashed into a giant Jackdaw nest, the Scarecrow covered Jack's head with his own straw body to protect him from attacking birds. Following their rescue, Jack and his companions traveled to the South Country to enlist the aid of Glinda the Good, ultimately witnessing the restoration of Princess Ozma to the throne of the Emerald City. He later attended the grand celebration held in the palace to welcome Dorothy to Oz.

label: Quote
value: Jack Pumpkinhead said: “My name is Jack Pumpkinhead,” returned the other, smilingly; “but as to my business, I haven’t the least idea in the world what it is.”

label: Quote
value: Jack Pumpkinhead said: “It seems to me that I have,” replied the Pumpkinhead, seriously; “but I cannot think what it is. My father knows all about it, but he is not here.”

label: Quote
value: Jack Pumpkinhead said: “But I hope she cannot get at us,” exclaimed the Pumpkinhead, with a shiver of fear. “She threatened to make tarts of me, you know.”

label: Quote
value: Jack Pumpkinhead said: “Oh, dear!” moaned Jack; “what an unhappy lot is mine! Why, dear father, did you not make me out of tin—or even out of straw—so that I would keep indefinitely.”

label: Quote
value: Jack Pumpkinhead said: “First, however,” said the Pumpkinhead, “I beg you will release me from this horse, and make me another leg to walk with. For in my present condition I am of no use to myself or to anyone else.”

label: History
value: Jellia Jamb originated from the North Country.
unit: Originating from the North Country, Jellia Jamb served in the Emerald City and was brought in by the Soldier with the Green Whiskers to interpret between Jack Pumpkinhead and the Scarecrow, using the opportunity to tease them before revealing they spoke the same language. During the siege of the Emerald City, Mombi magically disguised Jellia as herself to fool Glinda's surrounding army, though Glinda easily saw through the deception and demanded the real witch. She later attended the grand celebration at the royal palace in the Emerald City following Dorothy's arrival on the magic carpet.

After this conversation, Dorothy's party carefully travels through the region and exits over the opposite wall.

label: History
value: Princess Langwidere was a niece of King Evoldo
unit: Princess Langwidere was a niece of the late King Evoldo who ruled the Land of Ev and possessed thirty changeable heads stored in a cabinet. When Dorothy, Tiktok, and Billina arrived at her palace, Langwidere put on an ill-tempered head and demanded Dorothy's head for her collection; upon Dorothy's refusal, Langwidere had her army arrest the group and locked Dorothy in the North Tower. Princess Ozma of Oz later arrived at the palace and forced Langwidere to release Dorothy and her companions. When Ozma organized an expedition to rescue Ev's royal family from the Nome King, Langwidere declined to join the quest, remaining behind at her palace where she was eventually present when Prince Evardo was crowned the new King of Ev.

label: History
value: Mombi was an old sorceress
unit: Mombi was an old sorceress living in the Gillikin region of Oz who was taught magical tricks by the Wizard of Oz and obtained the Powder of Life from Nikidik. After returning home with new magic items, she used the powder to bring Tip's wooden creation, Jack Pumpkinhead, to life, but her plan to turn Tip into a marble statue caused the boy to steal her remaining powder and flee. She later aligned with General Jinjur to stop the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, conjuring magical illusions and confusing fields to impede their travel. When Glinda surrounded the Emerald City, Mombi attempted to evade capture through disguises and shape-shifting—including transforming into a rose, an ant, and a giant Griffin—before being pursued and caught in the desert. Under questioning with Glinda's truth-detecting pearl, Mombi confessed to having transformed the baby Princess Ozma into Tip, and she subsequently performed the incantation to break the spell and restore the princess to her true form.

After returning home with new magic items, she used the powder to bring Tip's wooden creation, Jack Pumpkinhead, to life, but her plan to turn Tip into a marble statue caused the boy to steal her remaining powder and flee. She later aligned with General Jinjur to stop the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, conjuring magical illusions and confusing fields to impede their travel. When Glinda surrounded the Emerald City, Mombi attempted to evade capture through disguises and shape-shifting—including transforming into a rose, an ant, and a giant Griffin—before being pursued and caught in the desert. Under questioning with Glinda's truth-detecting pearl, Mombi confessed to having transformed the baby Princess Ozma into Tip, and she subsequently performed the incantation to break the spell and restore the princess to her true form.

label: History
value: Nick Chopper was born a real man.
unit: Born a real man, Nick Chopper acquired his tin body gradually after experiencing numerous axe accidents, and he later destroyed the Wicked Witch's Grey Wolves before being invited to rule over the Winkies. He joined his old friends to help reclaim the Emerald City from General Jinjur's rebellion, aiding their escape by repairing Jack Pumpkinhead's leg with a table leg and constructing a flying machine called the Gump. During a later pursuit, a rose he wore was revealed to be the disguised witch Mombi, leading to her capture by Glinda. While travelling on a mission in Ev, Nick was transformed into a tin pig whistle by the Nome King until Billina recognized him and used a magic word to restore him to his original form.

During a later pursuit, a rose he wore was revealed to be the disguised witch Mombi, leading to her capture by Glinda. While travelling on a mission in Ev, Nick was transformed into a tin pig whistle by the Nome King until Billina recognized him and used a magic word to restore him to his original form.

For their wedding present, Gayelette gave him the Golden Cap, making Quelala its first owner; he then used its power to command the Winged Monkeys to forever stay away from his new bride.

label: Appearance
value: The Scarecrow is made of a blue, worn, and faded suit of clothes.
unit: The Scarecrow is a stuffed man made of a blue, worn, and faded suit of clothes packed with straw, featuring a straw-padded bosom and straw-stuffed shoulders. His head consists of a small sack stuffed with straw—which bulges out at the top—with a face painted onto it, including eyes, a nose, a mouth, and ears. On his feet are old boots with blue tops, and his hands are covered in padded gloves. Additionally, he wears a heavy golden crown set thick with sparkling jewels upon his head.

label: Personality
value: Scarecrow is driven by a persistent desire to get brains from the Great Oz.
unit: Driven by a persistent desire to get brains from the Great Oz and become as much of a man as any other, this figure originally journeyed to the Emerald City with a strong commitment to also help Dorothy get home to Kansas. He eventually attained the reputation of being the wisest personage in the Land of Oz, remaining calm under all circumstances, proud of his education, and maintaining a dignified, thoughtful, and philosophical nature. Happy, contented, and possessing a gay and charming expression, he considers brains to be far superior to money in every way. Possessing a body stuffed with straw, he does not need to sleep, rest, or eat, and he is able to see as well by night as by day. His selfless motivations include saving his friends, greeting his companion the Tin Woodman, and ruling the Emerald City until Princess Ozma is found, even endeavoring to regain his throne from the Army of Revolt. Despite his bravery in difficult situations, he harbors a deep fear of fire and lighted matches, knowing that a single spark could reduce his straw body to an ash-heap.

label: History
value: The Scarecrow is created by a Munchkin farmer.
unit: After being created by a Munchkin farmer and hung on a pole in a cornfield, the Scarecrow is helped down by Dorothy Gale and agrees to join her journey to the Emerald City to ask the Great Oz for brains. Along the yellow brick road, he helps rescue the Tin Woodman and the Cowardly Lion, and he uses his quick thinking to save the group from the Kalidahs and cross a deadly poppy field. Upon reaching the Emerald City, he receives an audience with Oz, who commands the party to defeat the Wicked Witch of the West before granting any wishes. During their quest west, the Scarecrow is destroyed by the Winged Monkeys, but he is later re-stuffed with fresh straw by the Winkies after Dorothy melts the Witch. Returning to the Emerald City, he discovers Oz is an ordinary man, but he accepts bran and pins as his long-sought brains and is made King of the Emerald City when Oz departs in a balloon. He leaves the city with Dorothy to seek Glinda's help, surviving encounters with China folk and Hammer-Heads before Glinda sends him back to rule his kingdom. Later, General Jinjur's all-female Army of Revolt overthrows the Scarecrow, forcing him to flee on the Saw-Horse with Tip and Jack Pumpkinhead to seek aid from the Tin Woodman. After escaping Jinjur's traps and building a living flying Gump, he is temporarily stripped of his straw by Jackdaws before Glinda restores order and crowns Princess Ozma, who commends his rich virtues of brain and heart. Subsequently, the Scarecrow joins Ozma's expedition to the realm of the Nomes to rescue the royal family of Ev. He devises a way for the group to bypass a pounding iron giant, but upon entering the Nome King's palace, he fails the King's guessing game and is transformed into a green ornament. He is later restored to his true form by Billina the hen, throws eggs to panic the Nome army, and mourns the loss of the Tin Woodman until his friend is successfully disenchanted from a tin pig whistle. Following their victorious return and a grand celebration in the Emerald City, the Scarecrow bids a affectionate farewell to Dorothy as she uses the magic belt to travel to Australia.

label: Quote
value: Scarecrow said: “I don’t know enough,” replied the Scarecrow cheerfully. “My head is stuffed with straw, you know, and that is why I am going to Oz to ask him for some brains.”

label: Quote
value: Scarecrow said: “All the same,” said the Scarecrow, “I shall ask for brains instead of a heart; for a fool would not know what to do with a heart if he had one.”

label: Quote
value: Scarecrow said: "and he would never hurt anyone who is our friend. If you will help us to save him I promise that he shall treat you all with kindness."

label: Quote
value: Scarecrow said: “I will return to the Emerald City,” he replied, “for Oz has made me its ruler and the people like me. The only thing that worries me is how to cross the hill of the Hammer-Heads.”

label: Quote
value: Scarecrow said: "How delighted I shall be to see my old friend the Tin Woodman again! I hope that he rules his people more successfully than I have ruled mine!"

value: The Nome King acquired the royal family of Ev from King Evoldo.

However, Billina discovered how to reverse his enchantments and freed the captives, after which the Scarecrow threw eggs at the King to exploit his fatal fear of them. Blinded and terrified by the eggs, the helpless Nome King was stripped of his magical belt by Dorothy, leaving him powerless as Ozma's party made their escape.

label: Quote
value: The King said: "Sit down, my dears," said the King, "and tell me why you have come all this way to see me, and what I can do to make you happy."

label: Quote
value: The King said: "Oh, no; you are mistaken about that," replied the King. "They are not my prisoners, but my slaves, whom I purchased from the King of Ev."

label: Quote
value: The King said: "According to the laws of Ev, the king can do no wrong," answered the monarch, eyeing a ring of smoke he had just blown from his mouth; "so that he had a perfect right to sell his family to me in exchange for a long life."

label: Quote
value: The King said: "That was not my fault," said the Nome King, crossing his legs and smiling contentedly. "I gave him the long life, all right; but he destroyed it."

label: Quote
value: The King said: "Of course not," the Nome King returned. "Nor will I give up the Queen and her children because the King of Ev destroyed his long life by jumping into the sea. They belong to me and I shall keep them."

value: The Queen of the Field Mice was rescued from a wildcat by the Tin Woodman.
unit: After being rescued from a wildcat by the Tin Woodman, the Queen of the Field Mice offered her gratitude and the help of her subjects to his companions. She gathered thousands of mice to pull a wooden cart, successfully hauling the sleeping Cowardly Lion out of a dangerous poppy field to safety. Later, she encountered the travelers again on their journey and lent twelve mice to hide in the Scarecrow's straw. She then guided the group past several of Mombi's magical illusions, leading them safely to the outside of the Emerald City.

label: History
value: Tiktok is a mechanical copper man.
unit: Tiktok is a mechanical copper man created by the firm of Smith & Tinker in Evna and fitted with Improved Combination Steel Brains. He is discovered locked behind a hidden door in the rock by Dorothy Gale and Billina, who use a golden key to wind up his separate mechanisms for thinking, speaking, and action. After introducing himself and explaining his background, Tiktok pledges his service to Dorothy and offers to guide her to Evna. Along the way, he defends Dorothy and Billina from the aggressive Wheelers using a tin dinner pail, capturing their leader and forcing him to act as a guide. Upon reaching the palace, Tiktok again defends Dorothy when Princess Langwidere orders her arrest, fighting until his action mechanism runs down, which leads to Dorothy's imprisonment. He is later introduced to the visiting Princess Ozma of Oz and agrees to join her expedition to rescue the royal family of Ev from the Nome King. During their underground quest, Tiktok enters the Nome King's palace to guess which decorative ornaments are the transformed royalty, but his action runs down during the attempt, forcing Dorothy to wind him up so he can finish making his ultimately failed guesses. After being transformed into an ornament himself, Tiktok is eventually disenchanted by Billina, escapes the Nome King's realm alongside Dorothy and Ozma, and attends the victory celebrations in the Emerald City before Dorothy bids her friends farewell.

label: Appearance
value: The Tin Woodman's body is composed entirely of pieces of tin.
unit: The Tin Woodman's body is composed entirely of pieces of tin, neatly soldered and riveted together into the human form, and features nickel-plated skin and nickel cheeks. He sports a funnel-shaped cap tipped carelessly over his left ear and wears a diamond necklace. When fully assembled and polished, his sparkling frame is accompanied by a gleaming axe carried over his right shoulder.

label: Personality
value: The Tin Woodman is kind-hearted.
unit: The Tin Woodman is a notably kind-hearted, sensitive, and proud individual who is devoid of vanity and greatly fond of flowers. He possesses an exceptional aversion to killing any living creature and maintains a consistently cheerful disposition, making him a popular favorite among the people. Initially, his primary drive was to obtain a heart from the Great Oz, believing a tender heart to be far superior to brains or education, so that he could love and marry a Munchkin maiden. He was eager to be of help to Dorothy on her journey home and aspired to rule forever over the Winkies in the Country of the West, whom he grew very fond of after they invited him to lead them. In addition to his strong emotional nature, he is a skilled mechanic capable of constructing machinery. He remains committed to using kindness in his dealings and actively seeks out paths, such as reaching the Emerald City.

label: History
value: The Tin Woodman was born the son of a woodman.
unit: Born the son of a woodman, the Tin Woodman grew up to become a wood-chopper himself and cared for his mother until her death. After a curse on his axe transformed his flesh into tin and he lost his heart, he spent a year standing rusted motionless in the woods until Dorothy oiled his joints and invited him to travel along the yellow brick road to seek a heart from Oz. Along their journey, he helped the group navigate dangerous obstacles, built a raft, slayed a wildcat to save the Queen of the Field Mice, and constructed a wooden truck so her subjects could rescue the Cowardly Lion from a poppy field. Upon reaching the Emerald City, he appeared before Oz as a five-eyed Beast and agreed to help destroy the Wicked Witch of the West. Though he was dismantled by Winged Monkeys during their search, Winkie tinsmiths later repaired his body, and after the Witch was vanquished, he received a silk heart from Oz. Continuing south with Dorothy, he chopped down aggressive trees, constructed a ladder to cross a china country, and was ultimately offered the rulership of the Winkies. When General Jinjur later usurped the throne, he joined the Scarecrow and Tip in seeking Glinda's help, accidentally carrying Mombi into camp while she was transformed into a red rose. After Tip was revealed to be Princess Ozma and took her rightful place as Queen, the Tin Woodman was commended by her and returned to his realm. He later joined Ozma's expedition to rescue the royal family of Ev from the Nome King, but after stepping forward to attempt the King's guessing game, he was transformed into a tin pig ornament. Left behind when his friends initially escaped, he was soon identified by Billina, disenchanted back to his true form, and happily reunited with the group to celebrate Evardo's coronation and Dorothy's elevation to Princess of Oz.

After a curse on his axe transformed his flesh into tin and he lost his heart, he spent a year standing rusted motionless in the woods until Dorothy oiled his joints and invited him to travel along the yellow brick road to seek a heart from Oz. Along their journey, he helped the group navigate dangerous obstacles, built a raft, slayed a wildcat to save the Queen of the Field Mice, and constructed a wooden truck so her subjects could rescue the Cowardly Lion from a poppy field. Upon reaching the Emerald City, he appeared before Oz as a five-eyed Beast and agreed to help destroy the Wicked Witch of the West. Though he was dismantled by Winged Monkeys during their search, Winkie tinsmiths later repaired his body, and after the Witch was vanquished, he received a silk heart from Oz. Continuing south with Dorothy, he chopped down aggressive trees, constructed a ladder to cross a china country, and was ultimately offered the rulership of the Winkies. When General Jinjur later usurped the throne, he joined the Scarecrow and Tip in seeking Glinda's help, accidentally carrying Mombi into camp while she was transformed into a red rose. After Tip was revealed to be Princess Ozma and took her rightful place as Queen, the Tin Woodman was commended by her and returned to his realm. He later joined Ozma's expedition to rescue the royal family of Ev from the Nome King, but after stepping forward to attempt the King's guessing game, he was transformed into a tin pig ornament. Left behind when his friends initially escaped, he was soon identified by Billina, disenchanted back to his true form, and happily reunited with the group to celebrate Evardo's coronation and Dorothy's elevation to Princess of Oz.

After a curse on his axe transformed his flesh into tin and he lost his heart, he spent a year standing rusted motionless in the woods until Dorothy oiled his joints and invited him to travel along the yellow brick road to seek a heart from Oz. Along their journey, he helped the group navigate dangerous obstacles, built a raft, slayed a wildcat to save the Queen of the Field Mice, and constructed a wooden truck so her subjects could rescue the Cowardly Lion from a poppy field. Upon reaching the Emerald City, he appeared before Oz as a five-eyed Beast and agreed to help destroy the Wicked Witch of the West. Though he was dismantled by Winged Monkeys during their search, Winkie tinsmiths later repaired his body, and after the Witch was vanquished, he received a silk heart from Oz. Continuing south with Dorothy, he chopped down aggressive trees, constructed a ladder to cross a china country, and was ultimately offered the rulership of the Winkies. When General Jinjur later usurped the throne, he joined the Scarecrow and Tip in seeking Glinda's help, accidentally carrying Mombi into camp while she was transformed into a red rose. After Tip was revealed to be Princess Ozma and took her rightful place as Queen, the Tin Woodman was commended by her and returned to his realm. He later joined Ozma's expedition to rescue the royal family of Ev from the Nome King, but after stepping forward to attempt the King's guessing game, he was transformed into a tin pig ornament. Left behind when his friends initially escaped, he was soon identified by Billina, disenchanted back to his true form, and happily reunited with the group to celebrate Evardo's coronation and Dorothy's elevation to Princess of Oz.

label: Quote
value: Tin Woodman said: “Yes,” answered the tin man, “I did. I’ve been groaning for more than a year, and no one has ever heard me before or come to help me.”

label: Quote
value: Tin Woodman said: “Get an oil-can and oil my joints,” he answered. “They are rusted so badly that I cannot move them at all; if I am well oiled I shall soon be all right again. You will find an oil-can on a shelf in my cottage.”

label: Quote
value: Tin Woodman said: “This is a great comfort,” he said. “I have been holding that axe in the air ever since I rusted, and I’m glad to be able to put it down at last. Now, if you will oil the joints of my legs, I shall be all right once more.”

label: Quote
value: Tin Woodman said: “I might have stood there always if you had not come along,” he said; “so you have certainly saved my life. How did you happen to be here?”

label: Quote
value: Tin Woodman said: “True,” the Tin Woodman returned. “So, if you will allow me to join your party, I will also go to the Emerald City and ask Oz to help me.”

label: History
value: Toto lived in Kansas.
unit: Toto originally lived in Kansas, where he loved to chase mice. He is carried away to the magical Land of Oz alongside Dorothy when a severe cyclone lifts their farmhouse into the air. Journeying along the yellow brick road, Toto travels with Dorothy and her new companions, though he succumbs to a magical sleeping spell in a poppy field before being carried to safety. Upon reaching the Emerald City and being sent to defeat the Wicked Witch of the West, Toto is captured alongside Dorothy by the Winged Monkeys, but they are freed after Dorothy melts the Witch. After returning to the Emerald City, Toto inadvertently exposes the Great Oz as an ordinary humbug from Omaha by knocking over a screen in the Throne Room. Later, Toto runs off just as Oz's hot-air balloon is about to launch, causing Dorothy to miss her ride home. Following a journey to the South Country and an audience with Glinda the Good Witch, Toto returns safely to Kansas with Dorothy via the power of her Silver Shoes.

label: History
value: Uncle Henry lived on a drab farm in Kansas.
unit: Uncle Henry lived on a drab farm in Kansas with his wife, Aunt Em, and his niece Dorothy until a severe cyclone struck, forcing him to tend to his livestock while Dorothy was swept away in their house. His health later broke down from working so hard on the farm, leaving him weak and nervous, so he embarked on a ship journey to Australia with Dorothy to recover. During a fierce storm at sea, Dorothy went on deck to look for him and was blown overboard. After spending time in the land of Oz, Dorothy used a magic picture to check on Uncle Henry, discovering that he was sick and lonely in Australia, which prompted her to have herself magically transported to his side to care for him.

His health later broke down from working so hard on the farm, leaving him weak and nervous, so he embarked on a ship journey to Australia with Dorothy to recover. During a fierce storm at sea, Dorothy went on deck to look for him and was blown overboard. After spending time in the land of Oz, Dorothy used a magic picture to check on Uncle Henry, discovering that he was sick and lonely in Australia, which prompted her to have herself magically transported to his side to care for him.

label: History
value: The Wicked Witch of the West spotted Dorothy and her companions traveling west.
unit: The Wicked Witch of the West spotted Dorothy and her companions traveling west to find her and dispatched wolves, crows, bees, and Winkie soldiers to destroy them. When her initial attacks failed, she used the Golden Cap to summon the Winged Monkeys to destroy the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, capture the Lion, and bring Dorothy to her castle as a servant. After attempting to starve the Lion, the Witch tricked Dorothy into losing one of her Silver Shoes, sparking an argument. In response, Dorothy threw a bucket of water on the Witch, causing her to completely melt away and freeing her captives.

value: Wicked Witch said: "Well, in a few minutes I shall be all melted, and you will have the castle to yourself. I have been wicked in my day, but I never thought a little girl like you would ever be able to melt me and end my wicked deeds. Look out—here I go!"

label: Quote
value: Wicked Witch said: “Go to the strangers who are within my land and destroy them all except the Lion,” said the Wicked Witch. “Bring that beast to me, for I have a mind to harness him like a horse, and make him work.”

label: Quote
value: Wicked Witch said: "Come with me; and see that you mind everything I tell you, for if you do not I will make an end of you, as I did of the Tin Woodman and the Scarecrow."

label: Quote
value: Wicked Witch said: “If I cannot harness you,” said the Witch to the Lion, speaking through the bars of the gate, “I can starve you. You shall have nothing to eat until you do as I wish.”

label: History
value: The Wizard is originally from Omaha.
unit: Originally from Omaha, the Wizard once worked in a circus before arriving in the land of Oz floating in a runaway hot-air balloon. Upon descending from the clouds, local residents mistook him for a great wizard; he then usurped the throne from King Pastoria, ordered the construction of the Emerald City, and hid the infant Princess Ozma away with Mombi, whom he taught magic tricks. While ruling, he encountered the Winged Monkeys in the Land of the West, an experience he had no desire to repeat. Seeking to return to Kansas, he eventually constructed a new hot-air balloon alongside Dorothy, but when its ropes snapped as Dorothy chased her dog Toto, the balloon carried him away alone, leaving her behind.

label: v3 · The Fate of the Tin Woodman
value: Dorothy steals the Nome King's magic belt.
chapter: v3 · The Fate of the Tin Woodman
unit: Dorothy steals the Nome King's magic belt while he is blinded by egg yolks, stripping him of his power to transform the group into scorpions. Using the belt, Dorothy reopens the passage out of the mountain and threatens the King until he tries to retrieve the transformed Tin Woodman, only to find the object missing. Giving up on finding Nick Chopper, the party escapes through the tunnel, using the belt to fend off pursuing Nome warriors and bypass the iron giant on their way back to Ev.

chapter: v1 · Chapter XIII The Rescue
unit: Dorothy frees the Cowardly Lion and informs the Winkies that they are no longer enslaved following the Wicked Witch's death. With the Winkies' assistance, Dorothy and the Lion retrieve the damaged Tin Woodman and the scattered clothes of the Scarecrow. Winkie tinsmiths repair the Tin Woodman, and the Scarecrow is re-stuffed with fresh straw. After a joyous reunion, the companions receive farewell gifts from the Winkies, and Dorothy claims the Golden Cap before they set out on their return journey to the Emerald City.

After consulting with the soldier with green whiskers, the group learns about Glinda, the Good Witch of the South, and resolves to travel south together to seek her help.

unit: Ozma and her companions reach the mountain edge of the Nome King's realm, where mysterious Nomes mock them. Dorothy manages to politely call forth the Nome King, who invites the group into his underground cavern palace. When Ozma demands the release of the royal family of Ev, the King refuses, showing off his vast army and revealing that he transformed the royal family into decorative bric-a-brac. He offers Ozma a high-stakes guessing game to rescue them, with the condition that she will be transformed into an ornament herself if she fails.

label: v1 · Chapter I The Cyclone
value: Dorothy lives in an environment in Kansas.
chapter: v1 · Chapter I The Cyclone
unit: Dorothy lives in a drab, gray environment in Kansas with her Uncle Henry, Aunt Em, and her playful dog Toto. A sudden and severe cyclone strikes the farm, prompting Uncle Henry to tend to the livestock and Aunt Em to take shelter in the cyclone cellar. Delayed while retrieving Toto, Dorothy is trapped inside the small house as it is lifted high into the air by the storm, where she eventually relaxes and falls asleep as it floats away.

unit: Dorothy lives in a drab, gray environment in Kansas with her Uncle Henry, Aunt Em, and her playful dog Toto. A sudden and severe cyclone strikes the farm, prompting Uncle Henry to tend to the livestock and Aunt Em to take shelter in the cyclone cellar. Delayed while retrieving Toto, Dorothy is trapped inside the small house as it is lifted high into the air by the storm, where she eventually relaxes and falls asleep as it floats away.

value: A fierce storm strikes the ship.
chapter: v3 · The Girl in the Chicken Coop
unit: A fierce storm strikes the ship carrying Dorothy and Uncle Henry on their way to Australia. Fearing her frail uncle has gone on deck in danger, Dorothy goes outside to find him, only to be blown overboard while holding onto a wooden chicken coop. Swept away into the sea, she manages to use the floating coop as a raft and eventually falls asleep once the storm subsides.

unit: Dorothy wakes up floating in the ocean inside a hen-coop and discovers a talking yellow hen as her companion. They introduce themselves, discuss the hen's ability to speak, and name her Billina before their coop finally drifts to a sandy beach. chapter: v3 · The Fate of the Tin Woodman
unit: Dorothy steals the Nome King's magic belt while he is blinded by egg yolks, stripping him of his power to transform the group into scorpions. Using the belt, Dorothy reopens the passage out of the mountain and threatens the King until he tries to retrieve the transformed Tin Woodman, only to find the object missing. Giving up on finding Nick Chopper, the party escapes through the tunnel, using the belt to fend off pursuing Nome warriors and bypass the iron giant on their way back to Ev.

value: General Jinjur summons Mombi.
chapter: v2 · Mr. H. M. Woggle-Bug, T. E.
unit: General Jinjur summons Mombi to help defeat the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, and Mombi uses magic to create a confusing field of whirling, face-bearing sunflowers that delays the travelers. After pushing past the illusion, the Saw-Horse trips in a rabbit hole and breaks its leg, leaving the group stranded while trying to figure out a repair. While sitting in the grass, the group is approached by the Highly Magnified, Thoroughly Educated Woggle-Bug, who introduces himself and prepares to share his backstory.

Tip reveals he has one last dose of the Powder of Life, so the Scarecrow suggests building a flying machine on the roof and bringing it to life. After Nick Chopper fixes Jack Pumpkinhead's leg with a wooden table leg, the companions set out to search the palace for materials.

unit: The group gathers various odd items on the roof to construct an escape flying machine. Led by Nick Chopper's assembly of sofas, palm leaves, ropes, a broom tail, and a mounted Gump head, Tip uses the remaining Powder of Life to bring the Gump creature to life. chapter: v2 · In the Jackdaw’s Nest
unit: The newly revived Gump converses with Tip and his companions before flying them all south toward Glinda the Good. During the night flight, Tip discovers a hidden compartment in the pepper-box containing Dr. Nikidik's Wishing Pills, though the strange instructions leave them unsure how to use them. At dawn, realizing the Gump has flown them completely out of the Land of Oz, Tip orders a landing on a mountain cliff, which results in a crash into a giant Jackdaw nest where the group becomes trapped.

chapter: v2 · The Scarecrow Appeals to Glinda the Good
unit: The travelers fly on the Gump to the South Country and arrive safely at the palace of Glinda the Good. They seek Glinda's help to liberate the Emerald City, but she explains that the throne rightly belongs to Princess Ozma, who was hidden by the Wizard. After studying her records, Glinda deduces that the old witch Mombi helped hide Ozma, and she resolves to march her army to the Emerald City to capture Mombi and uncover the truth.

value: Dorothy steals the Nome King's magic belt.
chapter: v3 · The Fate of the Tin Woodman
unit: Dorothy steals the Nome King's magic belt while he is blinded by egg yolks, stripping him of his power to transform the group into scorpions. Using the belt, Dorothy reopens the passage out of the mountain and threatens the King until he tries to retrieve the transformed Tin Woodman, only to find the object missing. Giving up on finding Nick Chopper, the party escapes through the tunnel, using the belt to fend off pursuing Nome warriors and bypass the iron giant on their way back to Ev.

value: Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion while traveling through a thick forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
unit: While traveling through a thick forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion who attacks the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, then threatens Toto. Dorothy slaps the Lion on the nose and calls him a coward, prompting the Lion to admit his secret lack of courage. He decides to join their journey to the Great Oz to request courage, and later in the day, the Scarecrow uses an oil-can to free the Tin Woodman's rusted jaws after the Woodman cries over accidentally stepping on a beetle.

Dorothy slaps the Lion on the nose and calls him a coward, prompting the Lion to admit his secret lack of courage. He decides to join their journey to the Great Oz to request courage, and later in the day, the Scarecrow uses an oil-can to free the Tin Woodman's rusted jaws after the Woodman cries over accidentally stepping on a beetle.

chapter: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

unit: The procession pauses so Billina can lay her daily egg, which the Scarecrow collects. Resuming their journey toward the Nome King's realm, they cross a deep gulf using Ozma's magic carpet and then encounter a giant iron man constantly pounding the narrow path with an immense hammer. Using the Scarecrow's strategy, the travelers time their runs under the falling mallet, safely bringing the whole group across after a few close calls and minor damages.

chapter: v3 · The Nome King
unit: Ozma and her companions reach the mountain edge of the Nome King's realm, where mysterious Nomes mock them. Dorothy manages to politely call forth the Nome King, who invites the group into his underground cavern palace. When Ozma demands the release of the royal family of Ev, the King refuses, showing off his vast army and revealing that he transformed the royal family into decorative bric-a-brac. He offers Ozma a high-stakes guessing game to rescue them, with the condition that she will be transformed into an ornament herself if she fails.

After saying farewell to all her friends in Oz, Dorothy is magically transported to Australia to care for Uncle Henry.

label: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
value: Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion while traveling through a thick forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
unit: While traveling through a thick forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion who attacks the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, then threatens Toto. Dorothy slaps the Lion on the nose and calls him a coward, prompting the Lion to admit his secret lack of courage. He decides to join their journey to the Great Oz to request courage, and later in the day, the Scarecrow uses an oil-can to free the Tin Woodman's rusted jaws after the Woodman cries over accidentally stepping on a beetle.

label: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
value: Dorothy and her companions camp in the forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

unit: The group uses the Tin Woodman's ladder to climb over a mysterious wall into a country made entirely of china, complete with fragile china inhabitants. Dorothy and her friends carefully journey through the china country to another wall, safely reaching the other side despite the Lion accidentally smashing a china church with his tail.

When the restored captives emerge, the King declares them prisoners, leading to a brief battle where the Scarecrow throws Billina's eggs at the King. Terrified by the eggs, the Nome army flees in panic, leaving the blinded King helpless as Billina tells Dorothy to seize his magical belt.

value: Dorothy steals the Nome King's magic belt.
chapter: v3 · The Fate of the Tin Woodman
unit: Dorothy steals the Nome King's magic belt while he is blinded by egg yolks, stripping him of his power to transform the group into scorpions. Giving up on finding Nick Chopper, the party escapes through the tunnel, using the belt to fend off pursuing Nome warriors and bypass the iron giant on their way back to Ev.

unit: As Billina repeatedly breaks the Nome King's enchantments, the angry King calls his warriors and tries to capture Dorothy, but the Sawhorse, Lion, and Tiger defend her. When the restored captives emerge, the King declares them prisoners, leading to a brief battle where the Scarecrow throws Billina's eggs at the King. Terrified by the eggs, the Nome army flees in panic, leaving the blinded King helpless as Billina tells Dorothy to seize his magical belt.

label: v3 · The Fate of the Tin Woodman
value: Dorothy steals the Nome King's magic belt.
chapter: v3 · The Fate of the Tin Woodman
unit: Dorothy steals the Nome King's magic belt while he is blinded by egg yolks, stripping him of his power to transform the group into scorpions. Using the belt, Dorothy reopens the passage out of the mountain and threatens the King until he tries to retrieve the transformed Tin Woodman, only to find the object missing. Giving up on finding Nick Chopper, the party escapes through the tunnel, using the belt to fend off pursuing Nome warriors and bypass the iron giant on their way back to Ev.

label: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
value: Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion while traveling through a thick forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
unit: While traveling through a thick forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion who attacks the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, then threatens Toto. Dorothy slaps the Lion on the nose and calls him a coward, prompting the Lion to admit his secret lack of courage. He decides to join their journey to the Great Oz to request courage, and later in the day, the Scarecrow uses an oil-can to free the Tin Woodman's rusted jaws after the Woodman cries over accidentally stepping on a beetle.

label: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
value: Dorothy and her companions camp in the forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

value: Dorothy and her companions camp in the forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

chapter: v3 · The Giant with the Hammer
unit: The procession pauses so Billina can lay her daily egg, which the Scarecrow collects. Resuming their journey toward the Nome King's realm, they cross a deep gulf using Ozma's magic carpet and then encounter a giant iron man constantly pounding the narrow path with an immense hammer. Using the Scarecrow's strategy, the travelers time their runs under the falling mallet, safely bringing the whole group across after a few close calls and minor damages.

chapter: v3 · The Nome King
unit: Ozma and her companions reach the mountain edge of the Nome King's realm, where mysterious Nomes mock them. Dorothy manages to politely call forth the Nome King, who invites the group into his underground cavern palace. When Ozma demands the release of the royal family of Ev, the King refuses, showing off his vast army and revealing that he transformed the royal family into decorative bric-a-brac. He offers Ozma a high-stakes guessing game to rescue them, with the condition that she will be transformed into an ornament herself if she fails.

unit: The group uses the Tin Woodman's ladder to climb over a mysterious wall into a country made entirely of china, complete with fragile china inhabitants. Dorothy and her friends carefully journey through the china country to another wall, safely reaching the other side despite the Lion accidentally smashing a china church with his tail.

Once the Lion is rescued to safety and Dorothy wakes up to thank them, the mice depart and the companions wait for the Lion to awaken.

chapter: v3 · The Heads of Langwidere
unit: Tiktok defends Dorothy and Billina from the Wheelers using a tin dinner pail, capturing the Wheeler leader and learning the secret that Wheelers only pretend to be fierce. The captured Wheeler guides them to the royal palace in the Land of Ev and explains the unusual nature of Princess Langwidere, who possesses thirty changeable heads. After being admitted by the maid Nanda, Princess Langwidere selects head No. 17 from her cabinet before going to meet her visitors in the drawing-room.

label: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
value: Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion while traveling through a thick forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
unit: While traveling through a thick forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion who attacks the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, then threatens Toto. Dorothy slaps the Lion on the nose and calls him a coward, prompting the Lion to admit his secret lack of courage. He decides to join their journey to the Great Oz to request courage, and later in the day, the Scarecrow uses an oil-can to free the Tin Woodman's rusted jaws after the Woodman cries over accidentally stepping on a beetle.

label: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
value: Dorothy and her companions camp in the forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

value: The travelers attempt to cross the river on a raft.

unit: The travelers attempt to cross the river on a raft, but the swift current sweeps them off course and leaves the Scarecrow stuck on a pole. Continuing their journey through a field of deadly scarlet poppies, Dorothy, Toto, and the Lion succumb to the flowers' magical sleeping spell, forcing the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman to carry Dorothy and Toto to safety while leaving the heavy Lion behind.

value: Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion while traveling through a thick forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
unit: While traveling through a thick forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion who attacks the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, then threatens Toto. Dorothy slaps the Lion on the nose and calls him a coward, prompting the Lion to admit his secret lack of courage. He decides to join their journey to the Great Oz to request courage, and later in the day, the Scarecrow uses an oil-can to free the Tin Woodman's rusted jaws after the Woodman cries over accidentally stepping on a beetle.

label: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
value: Dorothy and her companions camp in the forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

unit: The group uses the Tin Woodman's ladder to climb over a mysterious wall into a country made entirely of china, complete with fragile china inhabitants. Dorothy and her friends carefully journey through the china country to another wall, safely reaching the other side despite the Lion accidentally smashing a china church with his tail.

unit: General Jinjur refuses to step down, prompting Glinda and Princess Ozma to launch an aerial assault using the Gump to enter the Emerald City and capture her. chapter: v2 · The Astonishing Flight of the Gump
unit: The group gathers various odd items on the roof to construct an escape flying machine. Led by Nick Chopper's assembly of sofas, palm leaves, ropes, a broom tail, and a mounted Gump head, Tip uses the remaining Powder of Life to bring the Gump creature to life. After a wild burst of flapping nearly blows them off the roof, Tip successfully commands the newly animated Gump to return and settle back down.

chapter: v2 · In the Jackdaw’s Nest
unit: The newly revived Gump converses with Tip and his companions before flying them all south toward Glinda the Good. During the night flight, Tip discovers a hidden compartment in the pepper-box containing Dr. Nikidik's Wishing Pills, though the strange instructions leave them unsure how to use them. At dawn, realizing the Gump has flown them completely out of the Land of Oz, Tip orders a landing on a mountain cliff, which results in a crash into a giant Jackdaw nest where the group becomes trapped.

unit: General Jinjur summons Mombi to help defeat the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, and Mombi uses magic to create a confusing field of whirling, face-bearing sunflowers that delays the travelers. chapter: v2 · The Scarecrow Appeals to Glinda the Good
unit: The travelers fly on the Gump to the South Country and arrive safely at the palace of Glinda the Good. They seek Glinda's help to liberate the Emerald City, but she explains that the throne rightly belongs to Princess Ozma, who was hidden by the Wizard. After studying her records, Glinda deduces that the old witch Mombi helped hide Ozma, and she resolves to march her army to the Emerald City to capture Mombi and uncover the truth.

unit: The travelers fly on the Gump to the South Country and arrive safely at the palace of Glinda the Good. They seek Glinda's help to liberate the Emerald City, but she explains that the throne rightly belongs to Princess Ozma, who was hidden by the Wizard. After studying her records, Glinda deduces that the old witch Mombi helped hide Ozma, and she resolves to march her army to the Emerald City to capture Mombi and uncover the truth.

chapter: v2 · The Scarecrow Appeals to Glinda the Good
unit: The travelers fly on the Gump to the South Country and arrive safely at the palace of Glinda the Good. They seek Glinda's help to liberate the Emerald City, but she explains that the throne rightly belongs to Princess Ozma, who was hidden by the Wizard. After studying her records, Glinda deduces that the old witch Mombi helped hide Ozma, and she resolves to march her army to the Emerald City to capture Mombi and uncover the truth.

unit: In Glinda's tent, the Sorceress realizes the rose worn by Nick Chopper is actually Mombi in disguise. Mombi repeatedly changes shape—from a shadow to an ant, then to a massive Griffin—and breaks free, prompting Glinda to chase her across the desert on the Sawhorse while Tip and the others follow in the Gump. Mombi eventually collapses from exhaustion in the sands, where Glinda uses a golden thread to undo the transformation and capture the old Witch.

label: v2 · The Riches of Content
value: General Jinjur refuses to step down.
chapter: v2 · The Riches of Content
unit: General Jinjur refuses to step down, prompting Glinda and Princess Ozma to launch an aerial assault using the Gump to enter the Emerald City and capture her. With the Revolt ended, Ozma is crowned Queen, restoring order to the kingdom and dismantling the Gump upon its own request. Before the Tin Woodman and the Scarecrow depart for the Winkie country, Ozma commends them for their rich virtues of heart and brain.

value: The Woggle-Bug explains his origin.
chapter: v2 · A Highly Magnified History
unit: The Woggle-Bug explains his origin, how he gained education by listening to a schoolmaster, and how he became enlarged after being displayed on a magnifying screen. He accepts an invitation from Tip and the group to join them on their journey to the Emerald City. When the issue of the Saw-Horse's broken leg arises, the Woggle-Bug suggests using one of Jack Pumpkinhead's legs to fix it, allowing the party to resume their travel.

unit: The Scarecrow and his allies enter the Emerald City and march to the royal palace, where they find General Jinjur occupying the throne. The Scarecrow releases mice hidden in his straw, causing the female rebels and Jinjur to flee in panic, allowing the group to secure the palace doors.

unit: The group gathers various odd items on the roof to construct an escape flying machine. Led by Nick Chopper's assembly of sofas, palm leaves, ropes, a broom tail, and a mounted Gump head, Tip uses the remaining Powder of Life to bring the Gump creature to life. After a wild burst of flapping nearly blows them off the roof, Tip successfully commands the newly animated Gump to return and settle back down.
